concept: Return to the same office conflict, but change what sits between the colleagues: a judgement about Jordan becomes a verifiable work record, then a shared plan. The camera progresses from an uncomfortable desk tableau to the language, the workflow consequences, the agreed habit, the learner's choice and finally the opening desk working well. The governing world is a literal shared work surface, not a forced metaphor. It fits the conversation and its artifacts, supports visible changes and close details, and does not caricature either colleague.
world: One everyday office, with recurring desk, conversation table, project board and calendar bays. Jordan and an unnamed colleague, the learner's stand-in, recur in the imagined cases. Avatar bookends narrate outside the imagined action. Small designed acting rigs use posture and a single purposeful gesture; faces receive closer framing only with a designed expressive rig. Papers, schedules and speech slips carry the information. Refresh the pictured environment or its active nested region about every 15 to 20 seconds, while retaining the same station and object coordinates across a mechanism. In the long choice beat, change the framing from the calendar context to the option sheet without rearranging the choices. No numerical score for comfort, defensiveness or trust.
look: Selected story-cartoon: rounded forms, warm paper fields, dark ink outlines, flat fills and one crisp cel shade. Use the seed's paper panels, wobbly speech bubbles, underlined labels, boxed marks, bare icons and restrained paper finish. Definitions and evidence are calm; acting, dividers and payoff may use short drop arrivals with springy overshoot. Camera normally holds, with a purposeful lateral pan between work objects rather than perpetual movement. Clothes and background props stay muted. The pack's rust accent always means the work object or phrase currently being discussed, never blame, failure or success. Shape and wording distinguish those states. No red-versus-green verdict system, dramatic depth or unverified figurative drawing.

devices.what: A recognisable office desk tableau returns with the delayed document and unresolved schedule, then the same framing returns with an on-time release and open collaborative posture. Avatar bookends use its framing system.

A paper speech slip and adjacent work-record slot hold the current wording. Use the D-114 swap slot to replace or mark wording in place, and shape morph only when stacked phrasing becomes a direct message or a workflow object. Definitions and comparisons use settled states, not animated reasoning.

The same deliverable, milestone and downstream work objects make operational consequences tangible. Dependency counts, when spoken, are individual approval tokens, not bare numerals. Use D-114 data as objects. No invented dates, quantities, scores or automation.

A held planning surface has physical slots for an action, impact, perspective and agreed plan. The plan contains a habit slip and a calendar checkpoint. Reuse the lesson's actual objects for consolidation. D-114 stepped time moves a commitment into its relative calendar position, without implying an unspoken date or duration.

Jordan and the colleague change from facing one another across a judgement to looking at the same work artifact. Designed rigs provide small posed people and, if available, an asset-based pointing hand. A single gesture or listening pose accompanies the relevant verb; no comic humiliation or improvised anatomical drawing.

The join material is office paper. D-114 handoff carries a work slip into a pocket rule; an illustrated page join turns the choice sheet into the workflow preview. These joins mean taking the idea forward inside a topic. Today's fallback is a hard cut that preserves the paper's position. Chapter boundaries always remain hard cuts.

join_material: Office paper, shared across speech slips, work records and calendar leaves. Use built-in handoff or page only inside a topic, with cut as fallback. Use continue for a held mechanism, hard cuts for chapters and the later-time payoff. No zoom is planned, because no destination needs an object-entry move.

Each beat's line names a selected option and a same-allocation alternative. These are choices for pass 2, not permission to overwrite the selected story-cartoon look or the required avatar, template and motion treatments.
open_questions: No external knowledge-sheet or source verification was available through the supplied tools. This outline uses the supplied script for factual content, with Jordan's cases explicitly imagined. It does not independently verify claims about feedback outcomes.

Full scene rendering, encoded paper finish, actual avatar appearance, character-rig compatibility and hand-pose availability have not been verified at outline altitude. Pass 2 must check designed assets before using gestures; use non-figurative object emphasis if a pose is unavailable.

Those unsupported visual details are not planned.
